> For an index of all Next.js documentation, see [/docs/14/llms.txt](/docs/14/llms.txt).
Next.js comes with a variety of built-in optimizations designed to improve your application's speed and [Core Web Vitals](https://web.dev/vitals/). This guide will cover the optimizations you can leverage to enhance your user experience.

The Link Component prefetches pages in the background, for faster and smoother page transitions. * **Scripts**: Built on the native `

sections.heading: Metadata
sections.text:
Metadata helps search engines understand your content better (which can result in better SEO), and allows you to customize how your content is presented on social media, helping you create a more engaging and consistent user experience across various platforms.

The Metadata API in Next.js allows you to modify the `<head>` element of a page. You can configure metadata in two ways:

* **Config-based Metadata**: Export a [static `metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) or a dynamic [`generateMetadata` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#generatemetadata-function) in a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
* **File-based Metadata**: Add static or dynamically generated special files to route segments.

Additionally, you can create dynamic Open Graph Images using JSX and CSS with [imageResponse](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/image-response) constructor.

sections.heading: Analytics and Monitoring
sections.text:
For large applications, Next.js integrates with popular analytics and monitoring tools to help you understand how your application is performing. Learn more in the  [OpenTelemetry](/docs/pages/building-your-application/optimizing/open-telemetry) and [Instrumentation](/docs/pages/building-your-application/optimizing/instrumentation) guides.

- [Images](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/images)
  - Optimize your images with the built-in `next/image` component.
- [Fonts](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/fonts)
  - Optimize your application's web fonts with the built-in `next/font` loaders.
- [Scripts](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/scripts)
  - Optimize 3rd party scripts with the built-in Script component.
- [Metadata](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/metadata)
  - Use the Metadata API to define metadata in any layout or page.
- [Static Assets](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/static-assets)
  - Next.js allows you to serve static files, like images, in the public directory. You can learn how it works here.
- [Bundle Analyzer](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/bundle-analyzer)
  - Analyze the size of your JavaScript bundles using the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin.
- [Lazy Loading](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/lazy-loading)
  - Lazy load imported libraries and React Components to improve your application's loading performance.
- [Analytics](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/analytics)
  - Measure and track page performance using Next.js Speed Insights
- [Instrumentation](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/instrumentation)
  - Learn how to use instrumentation to run code at server startup in your Next.js app
- [OpenTelemetry](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/open-telemetry)
  - Learn how to instrument your Next.js app with OpenTelemetry.
- [Third Party Libraries](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/third-party-libraries)
  - Optimize the performance of third-party libraries in your application with the `@next/third-parties` package.

---

skill_drafts.name: Static Asset Serving via Public Folder
skill_drafts.description: Configure and serve static assets (images, fonts, files) through Next.js `/public` folder with CDN caching for efficient delivery.
skill_drafts.objective: Enable efficient static asset delivery with CDN caching
applicable_signals: Project requires serving images, fonts, or other static files
Assets should be cached and delivered efficiently across CDN
Static files are not expected to change per request
contraindications: Assets require dynamic generation or server-side processing
Content must be customized per request or user
Files need to be generated at runtime
workflow_steps: Create or use existing `/public` folder at project root
Place static asset files (images, fonts, etc.) in `/public`
Reference assets in code using root-relative URLs (e.g., `/filename.ext`)
Verify CDN provider caching headers are applied to `/public` assets
Test asset delivery and caching behavior in production
triggers: Project requires serving images, fonts, or other static files that should be cached and delivered efficiently across CDN.
constraints: Assets must be static and not require per-request modification
File paths are exposed in URLs; do not place sensitive files in `/public`
output_contract: Static assets placed in `/public` folder are accessible via root-relative URLs and cached by CDN providers for efficient delivery.

metadata.prompt: Place static assets (images, fonts, other files) in the `/public` folder at the project root. Files in `/public` are served at root-relative URLs (e.g., `/image.png` for `/public/image.png`) and can be cached by CDN providers for efficient delivery. Use this approach for assets that do not require dynamic generation or per-request customization.

skill_drafts.name: Image Component Optimization
skill_drafts.description: Optimize image delivery by implementing lazy loading and automatic device-based resizing. Use when rendering images in responsive web layouts to reduce initial page load time and improve performance.
applicable_signals: rendering images in responsive web layouts
need to reduce initial page load time
multiple images on a single page
images of varying sizes across device breakpoints
contraindications: static images with fixed dimensions that do not require responsiveness
images already served from CDN with built-in optimization
critical above-the-fold images where lazy loading would delay visibility
intervention_moves: Replace native elements with Image Component
Verify lazy-load behavior on viewport entry
workflow_steps: Identify images in the layout that would benefit from lazy loading and responsive resizing
Replace native tags with Image Component
Configure device-based sizing parameters
Test lazy-load behavior and responsive resizing across target devices
triggers: displaying images in responsive web layouts; need to reduce initial page load time
constraints: Image Component must be used instead of native tags to enable optimization
Device size detection must be available in the rendering environment
cautions: Lazy loading may delay image visibility; consider eager loading for critical above-the-fold images
Automatic resizing requires device size context; verify breakpoint configuration matches design requirements
output_contract: Images load lazily on viewport entry; image dimensions adapt to device screen size without layout shift; page load time is reduced compared to native implementation.

metadata.prompt: Apply the Image Component to abstract image optimization complexity. The component lazy-loads images on viewport entry and automatically resizes based on device screen size. Ensure images are wrapped with the Image Component rather than native tags to enable these optimizations.

skill_drafts.name: Link Prefetching Strategy
skill_drafts.description: Prefetch linked pages in the background to enable faster and smoother page transitions. Use when implementing internal page links to reduce perceived latency during navigation.
applicable_signals: Internal link element detected
Page transition latency is a performance concern
User interaction with link is imminent
contraindications: External links to third-party domains
Links to heavy resources that should not be preloaded
Bandwidth-constrained or metered network environments
User has disabled prefetching preferences
workflow_steps: Identify internal navigation links in the application
Configure Link component to prefetch target page resources
Trigger prefetch on user hover or focus event
Complete page transition on user click without additional loading
triggers: User implements internal page links in single-page or multi-page application
Goal is to reduce perceived latency on page transitions
Navigation between application pages is frequent
constraints: Only prefetch internal links within the application
Respect user network conditions and data-saver preferences
Do not prefetch resources that are not necessary for immediate page load
cautions: Excessive prefetching may consume unnecessary bandwidth
Monitor prefetch success rate to avoid wasted resources
output_contract: Target page resources are prefetched before user click; page transition completes without visible loading delay.

metadata.prompt: When a user hovers over or focuses on an internal link, prefetch the target page's resources in the background. This allows the page transition to complete without visible loading delay when the user clicks. Do not prefetch external links or heavy resources in bandwidth-constrained environments.

skill_drafts.name: Third-Party Script Loading Control
skill_drafts.description: Manage loading and execution timing of third-party scripts to prevent performance degradation and blocking of the main thread. Use when integrating analytics, ads, or external services that do not block initial page render.

skill_drafts.name: Next.js Image Optimization
skill_drafts.description: Optimize images in Next.js applications using the built-in `next/image` component to reduce file size, improve load performance, and enable responsive sizing with automatic format conversion.
applicable_signals: Multiple image assets in application
Performance metrics show image payload as bottleneck
Need for responsive image delivery across device sizes
contraindications: Images already optimized externally or via third-party CDN with no Next.js integration required
Static images served directly from public directory without component wrapping
workflow_steps: Import Image component from next/image
Replace standard tags with component
Set src, alt, width, and height props (or use fill layout)
Optionally configure priority, sizes, or quality props
Verify responsive srcset and lazy loading in browser DevTools

Format conversion (WebP, AVIF) is desired for performance

output_contract: Images are served with automatic format selection, responsive srcset attributes, and lazy loading enabled by default. Caller receives optimized image delivery with reduced payload and improved render performance.

skill_drafts.name: Third-Party Script Performance Optimization
skill_drafts.description: Optimize third-party scripts (analytics, ads, tracking) using the built-in Script component to control loading strategy and prevent main-thread blocking.
applicable_signals: presence of Google Analytics, ad networks, or tracking pixels
performance metrics show script-related rendering delays
build optimization phase or performance improvement initiative
contraindications: Scripts are critical for initial page render or above-the-fold content
Scripts are already optimized via external loader or CDN strategy
Script execution order is tightly coupled and cannot be deferred
workflow_steps: Identify all third-party scripts in the application
Classify each script by criticality: critical (beforeInteractive), standard (afterInteractive), or deferred (lazyOnload)
Wrap each script with the built-in Script component and assign the appropriate strategy
Test page rendering and script functionality with each strategy
Monitor performance metrics and script execution timing
Adjust strategies based on performance data and functional requirements
triggers: Application integrates external scripts for analytics, ads, or tracking
Performance audit identifies third-party scripts blocking main thread
Need to defer non-critical script execution
constraints: Script component must wrap the external script tag
Loading strategy must match script criticality and use case
Verify script functionality after applying deferred loading
cautions: beforeInteractive strategy blocks page render; use only for truly critical scripts
lazyOnload may delay analytics or tracking data collection; monitor data completeness
Test script behavior across different loading strategies before production deployment
output_contract: Scripts are loaded according to assigned strategy; main thread is unblocked for non-critical scripts; performance metrics (LCP, FID, CLS) show improvement or remain stable; all scripts execute correctly and collect data as expected.

metadata.prompt: Use the built-in Script component to wrap third-party scripts and apply appropriate loading strategies. This prevents scripts from blocking the main thread and improves overall page performance.

skill_drafts.name: JavaScript Bundle Analysis and Reduction
skill_drafts.description: Analyze and reduce JavaScript bundle size using the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin to identify and eliminate unnecessary code. This workflow helps diagnose performance bottlenecks caused by large bundles and guides removal of unused dependencies.
applicable_signals: high initial page load time
large JavaScript payload in network waterfall
bundle size growth over time
contraindications: bundle size is already within acceptable limits
analysis tools are not available or cannot be installed
workflow_steps: Install and configure @next/bundle-analyzer plugin in the Next.js project
Run the analyzer on a production build to generate bundle report
Review the report to identify large or unused dependencies
Evaluate each large dependency for necessity and alternatives
Remove or replace unnecessary packages
Re-run the analyzer to confirm size reduction
Test application functionality after changes
triggers: application bundle size is large
performance metrics indicate slow initial load
need to diagnose bundle composition before optimization
constraints: requires @next/bundle-analyzer plugin to be installed and configured
analysis should be run on production build output
changes to dependencies must be tested for functionality impact
cautions: removing dependencies without testing may break application features
bundle size reduction must be balanced against feature completeness
output_contract: Bundle analysis report generated; unused or oversized dependencies identified; bundle size reduced and verified through re-analysis
